reason: The reflector petals need a supporting frame, so the steel looks useful for building the solar furnace.
expectation: I expect a supported reflector assembly, though it may still need the receiver and tracking drive.

alternatives.reason: A framed screen could help prepare regolith feedstock, but I want to start with the furnace.

effect: The reflector is supported, so I can now attach the receiver.
reaction: The reflected patches moving together makes the assembly feel physically understandable.
reason: The receiver should collect the concentrated sunlight and advance the furnace goal.
expectation: I expect a more complete solar furnace, though it may still need tracking or other work.

alternatives.reason: The screen could help prepare feedstock, but I want to finish the furnace first.

effect: The solar furnace is complete, leaving feedstock preparation as the active goal.
reaction: The bright focal point makes the furnace's use of sunlight clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action and likely makes a screen for preparing feedstock.
expectation: I expect a supported screen for separating the excavated regolith, though further processing may be needed.

effect: The sieve is ready to separate the excavated regolith for feedstock.
reaction: The distinction between fine and coarse mesh makes its purpose clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action and should prepare the regolith for forming.
expectation: I expect finer regolith separated from larger stones, with further processing likely needed.

effect: The regolith is screened and ready for forming.
reaction: Separating the coarse stones is straightforward and physically clear.
reason: The press is the only offered gameplay action and should form the screened feedstock.
expectation: I expect the press to compact the regolith into a formed piece, though its exact shape is unclear.

effect: The press completes the feedstock goal, but the blanks still need firing to gain strength.
reaction: The distinction between shaping and bonding the grains was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Assembling the solar furnace was most worthwhile: the focused bright point and rising receiver temperature made its use of sunlight tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Screening the regolith was clear but somewhat routine, especially with only one gameplay action offered.

surprise.text: The pressed blanks remain weak and need support until firing; pressing gives them shape rather than finished strength.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the furnace and feedstock actions had clear physical purposes, although the later choices were prescribed by the menu.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see the blanks fired and learn what the resulting material can be used for; the physical explanations made that prospect interesting.
